text:
maria: Heads-up — after landing the bucketed freelist change we merged yesterday, I'm seeing a regression: a ~2x increase in GPU OOMs on shared-gpu-pool when KV prefill is enabled for long-history requests.

alex: can you paste a log or stack? which model/workload?

maria: repro on rw-demo-chat w/ seq_len 4096 and prefill=true. logs: 
```
E 03/13 09:10:12 gpu0_allocator.cc:214 OOM: failed alloc 12.8MB (requested for kv_prefill)
WARN 03/13 09:10:12 kv_cache.cc:88 prefill failed, falling back to decode-path
```

jin: hmm. bucketed freelist reduces contention but increases external fragmentation if we hold many medium chunks. Prefill allocs tend to request contiguous buffers.

sam: quick question: is the prefill path requesting one big buffer per request, or multiple small ones?

maria: single contiguous buffer for prefill for speed. decode path allocs are more piecemeal (kv-chunk size ~4KB).

yara: that aligns — fragmentation sucks for contiguous prefill. Did we enable any new workspace sizing behavior with the allocator patch?

maria: yes — we reduced max workspace slack and tightened alignment to 256 bytes to match kernel vectorization. That made medium-sized free spans less reusable.

leo: perf-bot just posted the deploy: 
"perf-bot: deploy 0.8.19 -> production at 2026-03-13T09:00Z (allocator-bucketed-freelist)"

jin: candidates to mitigate: 
- revert bucket sizes to previous config for medium bins 
- limit prefill to a per-request soft cap (e.g., 8MB) and stream the rest via decode path 
- implement coalescing on free list release (merge adjacent spans) 
- introduce per-request allocation arena for KV prefill that can be freed wholesale to avoid fragmentation of global freelist

alex: we should measure fragmentation to be sure. Maria, can you capture: total_free_bytes, largest_free_span, free_span_count, and wasted_by_bin before and after?

maria: collecting now. quick snapshot: 
- total_free_bytes=10.2GB 
- largest_free_span=1.9MB 
- free_span_count=18,452 
- wasted_by_bin (36-128KB bins)=~1.6GB 

sam: interesting — largest_free_span only 1.9MB explains the OOM for a 12.8MB contiguous request. Prefill should detect this and fall back earlier.

jin: suggested short-term patch: in kv prefill path, check allocator.largest_free_span() >= requested_size * 1.1 else fallback to decode-stream. Add a telemetry counter for how often we fallback. Low risk and quick.

yara: also consider small per-request cap: prefill_cap = min(16MB, request.expected_kv_size); if expected_kv_size > prefill_cap then prefill first prefill_cap bytes and stream remainder. This reduces contiguous demand.

maria: I'll prototype the fallback check + a 12MB default prefill cap. Would need canary and perf run.

leo: what about eviction strategy? Prefill currently pins into KV LRU with no per-request cap, causing eviction thrashing under memory pressure. We could mark prefill entries as lower-priority (age-bias on insert) and or use decode-prefill hybrid eviction.

alex: good call. Two orthogonal fixes: allocation-side fallback to avoid OOMs, and cache-side policy to avoid thrash. We should also rate-limit prefill concurrency per-GPU (like max 4 concurrent prefill ops).

perf-bot: perf run queued: rq/8721 (microbench: kv-prefill vs streaming, seq_len 4096)

sam: for longer term: allocator-level improvements — add a bucket coalescer that runs on low load and merges adjacent free spans; and consider a slab-like arena for KV that uses large mono-alloc blocks and returns them whole. That prevents freelist fragmentation when many short-lived prefill buffers are used.

jin: agree. slab arena also makes eviction simpler: evicting the slab frees many entries at once. But must watch GC pauses when freeing big slabs.

maria: action items: 
- [maria] add fallback check (largest_free_span vs request) + telemetry (prefill_fallback_count) — PR target EOW.
- [maria] implement per-request prefill_cap default 12MB and add config in runtime flags.
- [alex] add per-GPU prefill concurrency limit (default 4).
- [jin] draft design doc for slab arenas + coalescer.

yara: can we also add a short test in perf harness that ramps many concurrent prefill requests to surface fragmentation quickly?

maria: yes, I'll add a repro in perf harness and attach results.

alex: if the quick mitigations look good we can roll to prod with canary on shared-gpu-pool=10% then ramp.

maria: reassigning this bug to eng-runtime, label: kv-prefill-oom, severity: high. Will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

jin: thanks — love the approach (short term fallback + cap, medium term allocator coalescer + slab).

leo: keep an eye on latency impact from streaming fallback. If decode-path latency becomes too high we might need to compromise with a small contiguous prefetch + async rest via background fill.

maria: noted, will add latency telemetry and SLO gating for the canary.

alex: great. ping us when the perf results are in.
